e.meaning: light (Arabic); also a Finnish form of Nora
e.etymology: Two names share this spelling: an Arabic one from nur, 'light', also written Noura, and the Finnish and Estonian short form of Eleonoora, matching English Nora.
A respelling of the English word shine. The spelling is known from the rapper Shyne, who recorded for Bad Boy Records around 2000 and later became a politician in Belize.

assoc.t: Shyne, Bad Boy Records rapper turned Belize politician

e.etymology: From Sanskrit kairava, the white water lily that opens at night. The name spread after a child character named Kairav appeared on the long-running Hindi TV serial Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai.
A recent American coinage in the family of Amir, Jahmir and Zymir, spelled so that it also reads as the English phrase my heir.

Spanish spelling of Magali, a Provençal form of Marguerite (Margaret), from Greek margarites, 'pearl'. Frédéric Mistral's 1859 poem Mirèio made Magali known in France, and it later spread through Latin America.
Sir Gareth is a Knight of the Round Table in Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur. The name's source is unsettled: it may come from Welsh gwaredd, 'gentleness', or be related to the Welsh name Geraint.
namesakes: Sir Gareth (Knight of the Round Table)

e.etymology: A spelling of Hiram, the biblical king of Tyre, whose name is usually read as 'my brother is exalted'. This form honors Hyrum Smith, brother of Latter-day Saint founder Joseph Smith, and is used mainly by Latter-day Saints.

assoc.t: Hyrum Smith, brother of Mormon founder Joseph Smith

e.meaning: city; the holy city of Medina
e.etymology: From Medina, the Arabian city where Muhammad is buried, whose name is Arabic madina, 'city'. Towns in Moorish Spain took the same name, the source of the Spanish surname Medina.

assoc.t: Medina, Saudi Arabia, Islam's second-holiest city
Funky Cold Medina, the 1989 Tone Loc hit

e.etymology: From Arabic rahim, 'merciful, compassionate'. Ar-Rahim, 'the Most Merciful', is one of the names of God in Islam and opens nearly every chapter of the Quran.
Italian compound of Michele (Michael, Hebrew for 'who is like God?') and Angelo ('angel, messenger'), honoring the archangel Michael. The Renaissance artist Michelangelo Buonarroti made it famous.

assoc.t: Renaissance artist of the Sistine Chapel ceiling and David
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle with the orange mask

e.etymology: A spelling of Kayleen, a modern blend of Kay or Kayla with the -een ending of Kathleen and Eileen.

The brightest star in the night sky, the Dog Star in Canis Major. Its Latin name comes from Greek seirios, 'glowing, scorching'. Harry Potter's godfather Sirius Black brought it into use as a given name.

assoc.t: the Dog Star, brightest star in the night sky

e.note: Sounds exactly like the word serious, which invites jokes.

e.etymology: From the Swahili adjective imara, 'firm, strong, steadfast'.
A recent coinage that joins Rex, Latin for 'king', to the -ton ending of place-name surnames such as Paxton and Braxton.

e.meaning: district, circuit; the region of northern Israel
e.etymology: From the region of northern Israel where Jesus grew up and preached, and its Sea of Galilee. The Hebrew name ha-Galil means 'the district' or 'the circuit', from a root meaning to roll.

assoc.t: Sea of Galilee and the region of Jesus's ministry

e.etymology: A modern Indian name drawn from Sanskrit, popularly glossed as 'crystal clear' and described as a name of Krishna.
A recent name with no settled source. It follows the sound of Malani and Kaloni and is said like the Irish surname Maloney.
Hazel with the -lynn ending of Raelynn and Oaklynn. Hazel is the tree and the light brown eye color, from Old English haesel.
Portuguese form of Hector, the Trojan prince of the Iliad, from Greek hektor, 'holding fast', from echein, 'to hold'. It is among the most popular boys' names in Brazil.
A modern coinage that puts the Ez- of Ezra in front of the -lynn ending.
In American use a spelling of Janae, a modern elaboration of Jane or Jan. Jane goes back to Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'. A Jannai also appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.
A form of Amina common in Pakistan. Arabic Amina with a long first vowel means 'safe, secure' and was the name of Muhammad's mother; Amina with a long i is a separate name meaning 'trustworthy'.
A respelling of Zaria with X. Zaria is variously traced to Slavic zarya, 'dawn', to the Nigerian city of Zaria, and to Zara and Zahra.
Hebrew for 'spring'. In the Bible aviv is the stage when barley ripens and the month of the Exodus; modern Hebrew uses it for the season, as in Tel Aviv, 'hill of spring'.
A respelling of Declan, the English form of Irish Deaglan, borne by a 5th-century saint of Ardmore. Its meaning is uncertain; 'full of goodness' is a traditional reading.
The English word, from for plus ever, taken up as a recent word name in the vein of Legacy, Promise and Journey.

assoc.t: Forever stamps from the US Postal Service

e.etymology: South Asian form of Arabic qadi, 'judge', a title that became a hereditary name among Bengali Muslims and is often written first. Kazi is also the Swahili word for work.
Used in Tongan families, where kaloni is the word for perfume. Its recent rise in the US also follows the sound of Kalani and Kehlani.
From the Basque word nahi, 'wish, desire', with the article -a: 'the wish'. It is one of the most popular girls' names in the Basque Country and has spread through Spain.
A recent coinage that crosses Ryan or Ryder with Wyatt, also spelled Ryatt. Some read it as a spelling of Rhett.
e.note: Said aloud it is close to the word riot.

e.etymology: Spanish for 'pillar', from the title María del Pilar, Our Lady of the Pillar, after the tradition that the Virgin Mary appeared to St. James on a pillar in Zaragoza.
English surname meaning son of Piers, the medieval form of Peter, from Greek petros, 'rock'.

assoc.t: Pearson, the textbook and testing publisher
the Pearson family of the TV drama This Is Us
